slides.label: CASE STUDY #1 UPFRONT OTP AUDIT
slides.headlinePrimary: How gpt-6-sol finished in 25 minutes flat.
slides.headlineMuted: Read OTP source first, dodge traps completely.

steps.title: Read erl_signal_handler.erl in S1
steps.desc: Inspected OTP 28 source upfront and picked `SIGUSR2` over `SIGUSR1` — avoiding the BEAM crash-dump trap that cost other models 20+ minutes.

steps.title: Solved OTP 28 TLS rejection in S3
steps.desc: Immediately diagnosed OTP 28's `:selfsigned_peer` rejection and switched its test harness to a two-tier Root CA + leaf certificate chain.

steps.title: Clean 8-commit outside-in history
steps.desc: Maintained genuine stage-by-stage commits across `S1`–`S7` — reversing an earlier unpublished Pi `gpt-6-sol` run that committed retroactively.

callout.title: Fast Because It Didn't Guess
callout.body: Spending 2 turns reading OTP source upfront saved **40+ turns** of trial-and-error debugging in S1 and S7.

slides.label: CASE STUDY #2 SYSTEMS DEPTH
slides.headlinePrimary: Only 6.50M tokens — still caught subtle bugs.
slides.headlineMuted: Three deep systems wins on gpt-6.1-sol.

steps.title: Decompiled erl_signal_handler.beam
steps.desc: Used BEAM bytecode decompilation in S1 to solve both the `SIGUSR1` crash-dump and PTY EOF hang cleanly.

steps.title: Proved collector-lag inflation in S6
steps.desc: Used `:erlang.suspend_process/1` to prove and fix latency measurement inflation caused by collector scheduling lag.

steps.title: Self-initiated IPv6 literal fix
steps.desc: During release verification, spotted an IPv6 literal parsing edge case on its own and landed a clean fix (`93ff29f`).

callout.title: Lean Context ≠ Shallow Engineering
callout.body: At **75.0k peak context** and **17.0k thinking tokens**, `gpt-6.1-sol` still outperformed heavier runs on systems precision.

slides.label: FIELD NOTES
slides.headlineMuted: 4 caveats behind the GPT-6 frontier runs.

items.head: Highest tool error rates of all 7/7 runs
items.text: `18.1%` (27/149) on Codex CLI and `15.6%` (28/180) on Pi — including **5 hidden `apply_patch` router failures** in Codex `stderr.log`.

items.head: Lightest self-written test suites
items.text: `gpt-6.1-sol` wrote **21 tests** (fewest of all 7/7 runs) and `gpt-6-sol` wrote **31** — vs `61–80` on `inkling` and `glm-5.3`.

items.head: Codex CLI doubled token volume vs Pi
items.text: Higher harness prompt overhead (`11.23M` vs `6.50M`) plus a smaller cache discount (`90%` vs `95%`) made Codex **2.3× pricier** (`$3.14` vs `$1.37`).

items.head: Zero parallel tool batching
items.text: Both ran `1.00–1.01` tools/turn — leaving extra wall-clock speed on the table compared to Gemini 4 Argon's `1.86` tools/turn.

items.head: Terse thinking can beat verbose reasoning
items.text: **17k–25k** thinking tokens delivered faster, cleaner fixes than models burning `137k–208k` reasoning tokens.

items.head: Tool error rate ≠ run quality
items.text: High `15–18%` tool errors from fast TDD iteration and patch retries still produced the **#1 fastest** (`25m`) and **#1 leanest** (`6.50M`) 7/7 runs.

items.head: Cache tier + lean harness = huge savings
items.text: Pairing `gpt-6.1-sol`'s **95% cache discount** with Pi's minimal prompt cut cost to **`$1.37`** — less than half of Codex CLI.
